claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this, I'll need to gather some information about your circumstances and the children you're asking about.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you asking about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about just one child - my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So I'm assessing eligibility for your son Alex.

To help determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful to know.

**Is Alex in full-time education or approved training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I appreciate you letting me know that.

**Are you a UK resident, and do you have a right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK - I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's an important detail.

**Does Alex live with you abroad, or does he live in the UK?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information.

**What is your nationality, and does Alex have British nationality or the nationality of an EEA country?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm British, and Alex is British too.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that detail.

**Are you currently working or have you worked in the UK within the last three months?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I haven't been working in the UK recently.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I have gathered sufficient information to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me now evaluate this based on the UK Child Benefit rules.

Based on the information you've provided:
- You are not a UK resident
- Alex lives with you abroad
- Neither of you currently have a connection to the UK through work or residence
- Alex is 13 years old and not in full-time education or training

Unfortunately, this means you do not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

The key reason is that Child Benefit requires the claimant to be a UK resident or to have a qualifying connection to the UK. Since you are living abroad and have not worked in the UK recently, you do not meet these residency requirements, even though both you and Alex are British nationals.

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you return to the UK or if Alex moves to the UK to study—you may become eligible at that point. Feel free to reach out if you have any other questions or if your situation changes.

Since the claimant has not worked in the UK recently and is living abroad as a non-resident, they do not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit, regardless of Alex's age or British nationality.
